findings.description: Critical: Autopilot recovery specifies that unsafe teardown first clears the registry lease into quarantine and only then CASes the external envelope to checkout_state=quarantined. Present/teardown_pending envelope writes are gated on the live registry ownership triple, which is gone after that clear, and unlike the explicit identity-bound teardown_pending→removed CAS (envelope generation + lease_id + entry_generation + finalization_intent) the plan never defines authorization for teardown_pending→quarantined. A generation-only CAS would let a stale controller that reloads the latest envelope poison recovery state; requiring a still-live triple would make the legitimate unsafe-teardown path impossible.
findings.resolution: Define teardown_pending→quarantined as an identity-bound CAS using the same lease_id, registry_entry_generation, finalization_intent, and envelope_generation bindings as pending→removed (without requiring a still-live registry triple after the atomic quarantine-and-clear). Document that a wrong identity is a non-mutating conflict, and add a concurrent stale-controller fixture covering the unsafe-teardown path.

findings.description: Nit: contracts/mutating-skill-inventory.yaml classifies session-hooks as mutation_mode registry_reader and inherits defaults finalizer=teardown-or-quarantine / setup_owner=shared-phase-lifecycle. Design D10 and skill-workflow require session hooks to invoke only release-session as a non-destructive crash backstop and never phase finalization or teardown. Treating hooks as pure readers (or as teardown finalizers via defaults) will mis-shape inventory completeness tests and can authorize the wrong hook contract.
findings.resolution: Add an explicit session-release/backstop mutation mode (or equivalent), set session-hooks to that mode with finalizer=release-session-only and no setup ownership, and make inventory tests assert hooks call release-session, quarantine preserved checkouts, and never teardown or mutate autopilot recovery envelopes.

findings.description: Nit: contracts/cli/worktree-lifecycle.yaml setup-and-acquire both requires exact setup-id/generation/triple retry to complete or report success idempotently after reservation, checkout, evidence, publication, or response-loss crashes, and also says 'Refuse when an entry already exists; callers must use assessed acquire, resume, or explicit recovery instead.' A literal reading of the refuse rule breaks post-publication response-loss recovery that the worktree and skill-workflow specs require.
findings.resolution: Rewrite the refuse rule so it applies only to a pre-existing entry that is not the already-published result of this exact setup_id, entry_generation, and ownership triple; keep exact-match retry as an idempotent acquired=true success.

findings.description: Nit: coordinator-kanban-viz states that sync-point blockers are a live schema-v2 activity lease or a fresh legacy heartbeat, while design D15, worktree 'Provisioning reservation blocks sync points', active-agent tasks 1.5–1.6, and coordinator task 5.1 require unfinished setup reservations to be indeterminate non-activity blockers. Reusing the canonical active-agent check is helpful but the normative blocker enumeration still omits reservations and there is no coordinator scenario for them.
findings.resolution: Extend the coordinator sync-point requirement and add a scenario: unfinished setup reservations are indeterminate provisioning blockers, never active owners, and must appear in sync-point status without appearing in /worktrees/active.

findings.description: Optional: Task 0.5 and skill-workflow talk about packages declaring a feature-HEAD completion barrier, but work-packages.yaml has only prose on wp-baseline-preflight and the sole machine-readable signal lives in contracts/prerequisites.yaml (execution_gate.completion_visibility). openspec/schemas/work-packages.schema.json has no barrier field, so the scheduler declaration surface is easy to hardcode incorrectly.
findings.resolution: Either add a structured package field (for example completion_barrier: feature-head) that the DAG scheduler reads, or explicitly state that prerequisites.yaml execution_gate is the only declaration and that the scheduler keys off that package_id.

findings.description: Optional: Normalized LEGACY leases store controller_instance_id=null and may renew through the heartbeat compatibility handler without a controller, but lease release and teardown always require a non-empty controller_instance_id. Operators can clear those leases only via release-owner, expiry, or recovery adopt—not exact-triple release—which is workable but easy to miss beside the LEGACY renew exception.
findings.resolution: Document that LEGACY null-controller leases are released through release-owner/expiry/recovery, or add a narrow compatibility release path for the exact synthetic owner/lease with null controller, parallel to the heartbeat handler.

findings.description: Timestamp-free setup is implementable end-to-end: lease_intent omits acquired_at/last_heartbeat/expires_at, the registry schema rejects timestamped intents via additionalProperties:false, setup reservations advance reserved→checkout-created→evidence-created without granting activity, and the final locked publication derives all lease timestamps from one publication time before replacing the reservation with the active entry.
findings.resolution: Preserve reservation stage tests and publication-time lease construction as written in tasks 1.3–1.4 and the worktree scenarios.

findings.description: Live-lease ownership is consistently fenced across acquire, same-controller retry, resume with new fence after stale same-host evidence, renew/assert/release conflicts, teardown-before-release, atomic quarantine-plus-clear, session/owner bulk quarantine, and recovery adopt/force-adopt with null-target establishment and append-only force-adopt audit that survives entry teardown.
findings.resolution: Keep the exact-triple-and-generation command/output contract and the locked assessment order (refresh outside lock, revalidate generation/target under lock) as the implementation admission gate.

findings.description: Removed-checkout autopilot resume is exact-tip safe: durable_head and loop_state_sha256 are required for teardown_pending/removed, recreation demands current URL digest match plus freshly fetched ref tip equal to durable_head (not mere reachability), and the loop-state blob is hashed and schema-validated at that OID before worktree creation or lease acquisition.
findings.resolution: Retain advanced/rewound/missing/URL-mismatched refusal fixtures from task 4.3 when implementing recovery.

findings.description: The shared feature-HEAD preflight completion barrier is owned and sequenced: wp-baseline-preflight is a shared-mode root package, depends_on edges gate wp-pr-delivery and wp-phase-lifecycle, tasks 0.1–0.5 cover fail-closed PR evidence plus scheduler barrier behavior, and prerequisites.yaml names the blocked packages and dependent_base_rule.
findings.resolution: Implement the barrier in dag_scheduler/integration_orchestrator under the preflight package scope and keep the no-early-dependent-worktree regressions green before dispatching dependents.

findings.description: Delivery routing, append-only override invalidation, inventory coverage, and package DAG are coherent: the classifier truth table and merge-plan schema force stage-consistent routing, overrides are ambiguous-only with SHA/ruleset/JCS digest bindings, invalidation appends history before clearing, inventory enumerates standalone/continuous/child/sync-point/reader consumers with a dedicated migration package, and parallel package write scopes do not overlap once baseline and registry complete.
findings.resolution: Execute the stage-routing, override-history, inventory-scan, and package-validation gates already listed in tasks 2.7–3.10 and wp-integration verification.
